- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to reflect momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; apply a 1–2 period lag adjustment to downward revisions.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment support, consider mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days), model often fails to recognize downward pressure; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3–5 days, assume model is “overconfident” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days unless sentiment confirms upside.
